articles.title: Nature spaces 'need to be right next to where people live'
articles.summary: Campaigners are pushing for more wildlife-rich green spaces to be created within urban communities.
articles.body:
People should not have to travel far to experience the joys of nature, conservationists have said, as campaigners push for more wildlife-rich green spaces in urban areas.

From Greater Manchester to north London, organisations and volunteers are transforming former industrial land and neglected parks into habitats for wildlife and places for people to enjoy.

Research suggests many people do not have access to parks, woodlands or wetlands within a 15-minute walk of their home, despite evidence that time spent in nature can improve health and wellbeing.

Stephen Cartwright, from the Lancashire Wildlife Trust, said: "We need the places right next to where people live, that are scrappy bits of land."

If wildlife is to thrive alongside growing communities, campaigners said access to nature must become a bigger priority for policymakers and planners.

The Wildlife Trusts - a federation of 47 independent wildlife conservation charities covering the UK - has called on the government to improve people's access to nature.

Meanwhile a coalition led by the Horticultural Trades Association and the Gardens Trust wants trees, plants, gardens and parks to be recognised as essential infrastructure backed by long-term investment.

Across the country, projects have already demonstrated how green spaces can be brought closer to people.

At Cutacre, a former open-cast coal mine on the edge of Salford in Greater Manchester, the Lancashire Wildlife Trust has created meadows, wetlands, ponds and grazing areas with longhorn cattle.

The reserve is home to species including grey partridge, lapwing, skylark, grasshopper warbler and willow tit.

Conservationists have also reintroduced dyer's greenweed to Greater Manchester after the plant became functionally extinct in the area.

Cartwright said the reserve's location was one of its most important features.

Bordered by a housing estate, industrial units and communities in and around Salford, Bolton, Wigan and Manchester, the site offers nearby access to nature for people who may not otherwise visit a reserve.

"If you're a child growing up in a school over there, the majority of them won't travel to nature reserves," he said. "We need to bring reserves to them."

Cartwright's colleague Alan Wright, added: "We want to engage people in nature and the best way to do it is do things next to where they live. This is a perfect example."

More than 150 miles (241km) away in Tottenham, local residents have led the transformation of the Lordship Recreation Ground.

When the Friends of Lordship Rec group formed in 2001, chairman David Morris said the park was a neglected and unsafe space with derelict buildings and little biodiversity.

Today, supported by £7m in lottery and other funding, it features woodland, meadows, an orchard, food-growing areas, sports facilities and a restored watercourse.

The community group co-manages the park with Haringey Council and has helped secure its designation as a site of importance for nature conservation.

Morris said green spaces benefited both wildlife and residents.

"Being in nature has an amazing positive effect, immediate effect," he said.

He also called for increased funding for parks, adding: "Every neighbourhood should have access to a public green space."

The site now attracts volunteers of all ages and hosts activities including bat walks, birdwatching groups and events with schoolchildren aimed at encouraging a lifelong connection with nature.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: Brandel Chamblee declares USA’s Sunday singles performance best in team history — including Ryder Cup
articles.summary: Team USA's 17-13 fightback Presidents Cup is "their greatest Sunday singles performance" including Ryder Cups, according to Brandel Chamblee; watch the Bank of Utah Championship early coverage live on Thursday from 5pm on Sky Sports Golf ahead of full coverage from 10pm
articles.body:
Team USA trailed by three points heading into the Sunday singles at Medinah, leaving them needing eight points from the final 12 matches to avoid a first Presidents Cup defeat since 1998. They responded in spectacular fashion.

Cameron Young, Justin Thomas and Scottie Scheffler delivered early points for Team USA, before victories for Chris Gotterup, Patrick Cantlay, Collin Morikawa and Jackson Koivun - with Xander Schauffele already guaranteed at least a half against Ryan Fox - ended the Internationals' hopes of victory.

Jacob Bridgeman then secured the crucial point to guarantee Team USA would lift the trophy once again. He rallied from one down with three holes to play to defeat Min Woo Lee on the final hole, completing the biggest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history and sparking wild celebrations.

"The US team nailed it," Chamblee told the Golf Channel .

"What we saw today was historic - this is the greatest ever Sunday single performance, not just by a President's Cup team, but by a US Ryder Cup team.

"You go all the way back to 1979 in the Ryder Cup, the U.S. team had never won more than eight and a half points. You go all the way back to the beginnings in 1994 of the Presidents Cup, the US team had never won more than eight points.

"What happened today was what was predicted to happen all week long, given the disparity between the world rank of the international team and the US team."

Chamblee also suggested that the US team, who suffered defeat on home soil at the 2025 Ryder Cup, were motivated by a desire to prove their doubters wrong as they looked to avoid a second successive team-event defeat.

"But when you look at the final result, nine and a half to two and a half, and again, go back to 2025, the final day of the Ryder Cup - look at what happened today.

"In the final day of the singles at the Ryder Cup in 2025, Europe only won one match. Today, the Internationals only won two matches. So you're talking about 24 matches.

"It feels like to me that the US team is chagrined a little bit at some of the criticism coming their way, perhaps from the Ryder Cup lack of success.

"But in the individual performances, in the Sunday singles, what they did last time they were out at the Ryder Cup was historic."

Snedeker: Team USA will be a problem at Ryder Cup

Victorious Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker believes the United States team "is going to be a problem" for Europe at next year's Ryder Cup.

The 45-year-old received some criticism for his captaincy as they were staring at a first defeat on home soil after being dominated over the first three days at Medinah.

Snedeker believes that the eventual victory offers hope for the centenary edition of the Ryder Cup at Adare Manor in Ireland as they bid to win on foreign soil for the first time since 1993.

"It doesn't mean anything for me, it means more for USA golf," he said.

"I think we're all tired of this narrative that we don't care about each other, that we don't know how to play team golf. I think this proves it.

"You don't come back the way we did if these guys haven't all bought into each other. This team is going to be a problem in Ireland. It's going to be a problem."

The United States will be back in action next September when they take on Team Europe in the Ryder Cup, held at Adare Manor in Ireland from September 17-19. The next Presidents Cup will be held in 2028 at Kingston Heath Golf Club in Melbourne, Australia.

articles.title: Los datos de la Presidents Cup: Tom Kim el mejor y Koivun la revelación
articles.standfirst: El surcoreano Tom Kim fue el único que sumó cuatro puntos
articles.summary: El surcoreano Tom Kim fue el único que sumó cuatro puntos
articles.body: Jackson Koivun sólo tiene 21 años y este año estrenó su palmarés en el PGA Tour en el que era su tercer torneo profesional. El capitán estadounidense de la Presidents Cup, Brandt Snedeker, no dudó en incluir al joven talento en su equipo para que se vaya adaptando tanto a sus compañeros como a un formato de competición que conoce bien de su etapa amateur, pero que puede suponer una presión añadida. Koivun concluyó su participación con una actuación global de 2-0-1 (victorias-derrotas-empates) en Medinah y una victoria final en los individuales por 2 arriba, sobre quien posiblemente es la estrella de los Internacionales, Si Woo Kim. La experiencia adquirida no tiene precio si en el futuro forma parte del equipo de la Ryder. “Creo que nunca había temblado tanto en un campo de golf como el jueves en el primer tee”, confesó Koivun. El domingo fue un día decepcionante para el equipo Internacional, mientras que los estadounidenses remontaron para vencer por un marcador de 17-13 gracias a las actuaciones destacadas de jugadores como Koivun, Gotterup, Scheffler y Young. Tres integrantes del equipo americano consiguieron tres puntos (Gotterup, Scheffler y Young), pero aun así se quedaron a uno de los cuatro que conquistó Tom Kim. El surcoreano, que actuó en el segundo partido individual, puso rumbo a Japón para disputar los Juegos Asiáticos en cuanto terminó, donde aspira a obtener una medalla de oro para así poder librarse del servicio militar obligatorio de su país.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: Does Team USA's comeback win over Internationals show change is needed to make event more competitive?
articles.summary: The United States maintained their Presidents Cup winning streak over the International Team, with the latest victory reigniting debate about whether change is needed.
articles.body:
Brandt Snedeker's side produced the largest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history at Medinah, winning 9.5 of the 12 points on offer in the Sunday singles to close out a record-extending 11th consecutive victory.

A 17-13 winning margin doesn't tell the full picture from a closer-than-expected contest, including a foursomes session sweep for the Internationals on Friday and them leading going into the final day for just the fourth time ever.

The harsh reality, however, is that the International Team fell short again after threatening a shock victory, extending their wait for a first win over the United States since 1998.

Geoff Ogilvy's side were more than a match for the Americans over the first three days but were outclassed on Sunday, meaning Team USA have now won 14 of 16 Presidents Cups ever played.

"It was sort of on a knife's edge all day," Ogilvy said. "Some of those one downs that we had out there, if they'd flipped to one up, the numbers look really good and who knows what momentum can give."

Could schedule changes boost the Internationals?

The Presidents Cup is a four-day event with 30 total matches, which is a day longer and two matches more than the format used for both the Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup.

The disparity in strength of teams in the Presidents Cup is greater than in the two involving Europe, so could a tighter schedule of fewer matches be of benefit?

Playing foursomes and fourballs on both Friday and Saturday means fewer matches but more opportunities to bench weaker members of a team, plus puts less pressure on the marquee names to play in every session.

"They need to start the President's Cup on Friday and reduce the number of points," Golf Channel's Brandel Chamblee insisted. "Reduce it to 24. If they're playing for 28 in the Ryder Cup, why in the heck are they playing for 30 in the Presidents Cup when there's a bigger separation between the talent?

"If it were just 24 points, you would only need 12 and a half to get to a victory. The first three Presidents Cups were started on a Friday and if you go back and combine the points from 1994, 1996 and 1998, they [Team USA and Internationals] were dead even after those three.

"There's no point in it going four days, drawing it out. The longer you go out, the more the better players and the better team are going to come to the fore. That was evidenced very poignantly."

Should LIV Golf players be allowed to play?

The Presidents Cup being a PGA Tour-owned event immediately makes LIV Golf League players ineligible, which has had a bigger impact on the International Team's depth than it has on the United States.

The early years of the Presidents Cup saw the Internationals have former world No 1s Greg Norman, Nick Price, Ernie Els and Vijay Singh at their disposal, but their strength had already weakened before the emergence of LIV Golf.

Chilean Joaquin Niemann and 2022 Open champion Cameron Smith are two of the players no longer able to feature, with Lucas Herbert - who impressed this season - and International Team stalwart Louis Oosthuizen among the others who can't be involved.

"Give the Internationals autonomy to choose who they want," Chamblee added. "You're telling me they wouldn't have chosen some LIV players to be on this team?

"The PGA of America runs the Ryder Cup on the US side and the DP World Tour has their own set of rules, so it allows them to choose a Jon Rahm or - in the case of the US team - a Bryson DeChambeau.

"It certainly mattered to the European Ryder Cup team at Marco Simone [2023]. It would have mattered for this Presidents' Cup team, which has been gutted by six of the players that made 2019 so competitive going off to LIV Golf."

How about adding LPGA Tour stars to the team?

The idea of a mixed Presidents Cup has previously been suggested to make the contest more balanced, given five of the world's top six in the women's game - as of September 29 - would be eligible to represent an International side based on the current criteria.

"Maybe they [the PGA Tour] go into a partnership with the LPGA Tour to create something like that," former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley recently told Sky Sports . "Whether they do it for the Presidents Cup is doubtful, because they've already said no to that situation evolving.

"They may open up a new pathway for it, you never know, but it does make a lot of sense to do that because then you would get two really good, balanced teams. If you add half of the ladies internationally combined with the men, you would have a pretty formidable team that would be very strong against the might of America."

Any addition of female participation would offer its own challenges on the course in terms of tee positions and the formats used, along with schedule agreements and tour partnerships off it, but it's something Min Woo Lee would be open to see happening in the future.

"It would be nice to have her [Minjee Lee, his sister] on the team and me on the team - think it would be very fun," Lee said ahead of this year's event. "It would make it interesting, for sure. Even just the best ball, like mixed best ball, mixed foursome would be unbelievable."

Should the Presidents Cup go global more often?

The PGA Tour already offers an American-heavy schedule of events, so why not take their marquee team event elsewhere and show off their star players to a global audience?

Some 18 different nationalities have represented the Internationals at a Presidents Cup, including seven at Medinah, yet only four countries - outside the United States - have ever hosted the biennial contest.

South Africa, a nation with huge golfing history and one that produced huge crowds for a LIV Golf event earlier this year, hasn't held the Presidents Cup since the historic 15-15 tie in 2003.

Australia, Canada and South Korea are the only other previous other host nations, with the Middle East, India, Japan and New Zealand all potential golfing markets for the Presidents Cup to explore.

Always playing the Presidents Cup outside of the United States would take the PGA Tour to new areas and could inspire a new generation of international stars. Plus, more away matches could also help Team USA's bid to end a dismal Ryder Cup record on the road.

Could Europe help the International Team?

Europe have used a variety of different match play events to give players experience of playing in a team environment, but could one involving the Internationals be of benefit to both?

The now-defunct Seve Trophy and the current Hero Cup have been events where Great Britain and Ireland have faced Continental Europe, while the EurAsia Cup was a team competition previously played between Europe and Asia.

All three have given potential Ryder Cup players the chance to impress, with Ramsus Hojgaard featuring in the Hero Cup last January before making his Team Europe debut at Bethpage Black later that season.

While those team competitions haven't typically included all of Europe's marquee talent, a new competition would give the Internationals a bonus week together to experiment with different partnerships and prepare to face the United States.

The biggest challenge for his idea would be where it fits in the schedule, given the Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup take place in alternate years. Would an early-season slot - like the Hero Cup uses - work ahead of the PGA Tour campaign?

Should the golfing calendar get in the way of Europe providing the Internationals with another team tournament, could they create their own biennial event for the non-Presidents Cup years?

Asia vs the rest of the world, outside of Europe and United States? A Northern Hemisphere vs Southern Hemisphere team contest? A nation vs nation competition to bring together possible future pairings? There's plenty of fun to possibly be had.

We already have the Hanwha LifePlus International Crown on the LPGA Tour, a team tournament that sees different nations go head-to-head across multiple formats, but a similar event is currently lacking from the men's schedule.

One could slot into the post-season during Ryder Cup years, which is not administered by the PGA Tour, giving them another team event to sell globally and be another way to allow the International players practice of competing in team golf.

The Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup have both continued to grow in stature within the sporting calendar. Another Presidents Cup defeat for the Internationals means the contest may need to evolve and make changes to improve its own status.

The United States will be back in action next September when they take on Team Europe in the Ryder Cup, held at Adare Manor in Ireland from September 17-19. articles.title: Forest Green allow Savage to talk to another club
articles.summary: Forest Green give manager Robbie Savage permission to speak to another club, amid speculation linking him to Peterborough United.
articles.body:
Forest Green Rovers have given manager Robbie Savage permission to speak to another club, amid speculation linking him to the vacant role at Peterborough United.

The National League side added that Savage would not be in the dugout for Tuesday night's game at home to Wealdstone.

Asked on Saturday whether he had any contact from Posh, Savage did not deny the speculation but said he did not know if there had been contact from the club.

"I don't know, I've got a game to prepare for and I'm really excited to watch my team," he told BBC Radio Gloucestershire.

Former Wales international Savage was appointed at Forest Green on 1 July 2025, having previously managed non-league Macclesfield Town.

The 51-year-old, who played as a midfielder for clubs including Derby County, Birmingham City, Leicester City and Blackburn Rovers, guided Forest Green to seventh in the table last season but they were beaten in the play-off eliminators.

This season they sit 12th after 10 matches, with four wins, two draws and four defeats.

Peterborough are looking for a new manager after sacking Luke Williams on 19 September following a poor start to the season.

They are currently 23rd in League One with just one win in eight league games.

articles.title: Jersey's renewable energy focussed academy welcomes students
articles.summary: Highlands College and Jersey Electricity have partnered to launch the Green Skills Academy.
articles.body:
An academy set up for apprentices to learn skills that can help provide and support the use of renewable energy on the island has started welcoming students.

Highlands College and Jersey Electricity (JE) announced in February they have partnered to launch the Green Skills Academy.

The idea came about after a team member at JE noticed there was a need for better training, focussed on the sector.

Plumbing apprentice Corie Smith said: "I think there's nothing more special than being a part of the future and building a greener, more sustainable future up and around."

He added he wanted to be part of something "that's building towards the future".

"Previous to this I was just doing ordinary plumbing and normal heating, contributing in the best ways I could, and when I found out about this opportunity and I spoke to my tutor about it and I thought it was an opportunity that I couldn't possibly turn down."

Along with learning the plumbing skills, he said he gets to "contribute to the future of Jersey and the people around me, which I think is a beautiful thing".

CEO of JE Chris Ambler, said: "There was a recognition that there was a limited number of skilled individuals in green technologies in the marketplace, so we decided to seed the Green Skills Academy, and that's what we're opening.

"What we've built here is a state-of-the-art training system and yes, it's equipment but it's also the curriculum."

On the topic of apprentices, he added: "We're hoping we're going to produce 36 over the next three years, who will help install a lot more facilities."

Lance Chatfield, principal at Highlands College, said: "Apart from obviously this holistic approach around making sure they've got the qualifications they need, it's also having hands-on experience which is absolutely essential to them [apprentices].

"Understanding how the technologies work and around us we've got some of the best kit in the world, so we make sure they get hands-on with that kit."

He added: "It is groundbreaking and I would say exceeds most of the facilities I've ever seen across the UK and the rest of Europe.

"We are bringing this to the island to make sure that our young people and those wishing to retrain can come here, study and end up working here and stay on this island which is obviously key for the island's economy."

articles.title: PGA Tour Golfer Must Win Tournament to Avoid Military Service
articles.summary: Tom Kim will be competing for more than just a golf victory when he tees it up at the Asian Games starting Wednesday at Kasugi Country Club.
articles.body:
Tom Kim will be competing for more than just a golf victory when he tees it up at the Asian Games starting Wednesday at Kasugi Country Club.

Doug Ferguson of the Associated Press reported Kim has the opportunity to earn an exemption from his mandatory South Korean military service if he wins a gold medal in the men's competition or the team competition.

South Korean law requires able-bodied men to perform 18 to 21 months of military service, although exemptions are made for classical artists and athletes if they generate national prestige with their performances in international competitions.

A gold medal at the Asian Games or any medal in the Olympics earns such an exemption for athletes.

Kim had an opportunity to achieve just that during the 2024 Paris Olympics when he started the final round four shots behind the leader. However, he ended four shots outside of the podium with a 68 in that last round.

This year's Asian Games give him an excellent opportunity to avoid that military service.

Ferguson noted the Asian Games used to be for amateurs, but professionals were first allowed during the 2023 competition. Sungjae Im and Si Woo Kim led South Korea to the gold medal in the team competition by 25 shots.

Kim will look to replicate that victory this year after a solid season on the PGA Tour.

He made the cut in 20 of his 23 starts this season and won the Genesis Scottish Open in July. He also finished in third place at the U.S. Open in June and tied for fifth at the Wyndham Championship in August.

articles.title: Justin Thomas jokes that Jackson Koivun 'blacked out' at Presidents Cup while praising newest American star
articles.summary: Justin Thomas recalls the unforgettable moment Jackson Koivun "blacked out" on the first tee before the Auburn rookie went 2-0-1 at Medinah.

Nobody in the world had a better seat to witness Koivun's abilities with a golf club in his hand than teammate Justin Thomas, who thoroughly enjoyed the show the former Auburn star put on. Thomas and Koivun were paired together for what was the third match of the opening day's four-ball session. With this year's Presidents Cup marking Thomas' fourth, he's learned to take things in on the first tee, and he picked up on the fact that Koivun virtually "blacked out" before finding the fairway with his opening tee shot. "It just was really cool to kind of just watch him do his thing. I'll never in my life forget the smile he had on his face when he put the tee in the ground on Thursday morning and he was about to hit," Thomas recalled on Sunday. articles.title: David Stearns addresses the media after a disappointing Mets season
articles.summary: The Mets’ president of baseball operations spoke on regrets, optimism for the future
articles.body:
New York Mets President of Baseball Operations David Stearns held his end-of-season press conference today. The Mets missed the playoffs for the second straight year and finished last in the NL East despite a sky-high payroll and high expectations.

Stearns had to walk a tightrope with his answers, acknowledging his mistakes in building the 2026 squad while also sharing a message of optimism with a team that finished 34-31 after the All-Star break.

It didn't take long for Pete Alonso or the now-cursed phrase 'run prevention' forever associated with Stearns to be brought up. Still, the executive pointed to the team's improved cohesiveness after Andy Green took over managerial duties following Carlos Mendoza's firing, as well as the exciting young talent that flourished as the season went on.

"The disappointment of this season is very true and real. I feel that, we as an organization, feel that, our fan base feels that. There's no denying any of that, Stearns said. "There is also the real foundation here for the level of success and competitiveness that we expect to have, and that is also real."

The Mets' brutally slow start to the season, including a 12-game losing streak and injuries to Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor , was essentially a worst-case scenario for the club and stood out to Stearns when asked what he could do to make sure missing the playoffs in such mediocre fashion wouldn't happen again.

"We and I made a number of decisions that created the potential for almost an uncapped downside scenario," he said. "We had a lot of change. I think that change in New York is probably different than change in other markets. We lived that. I think in addition to that change, we had different elements of our roster that didn't have enough flexibility, so when we had underperformance, it made it very difficult for us to make in-season, on-the-fly adjustments."

With another season of missing the playoffs, and Mets fans quick to call for Stearns's scalp at games and online, he was asked if he feels pressure to turn it around.

"I'm always under pressure," he said. "My job is to put a winning team on the field every year. That hasn't changed from the day I sat up here for my introductory press conference to when I'm sitting up here right now."

Alonso's departure in free agency to the Orioles and his subsequent career year at the plate, combined with the Mets struggling to find a solid solution at first base, raised questions about what he learned from the situation.

"The truth is, in this job, I don't get mulligans. I also recognize that Pete had a tremendous year, and the totality of our production at first base wasn't good enough," Stearns said. "It's my job to ensure that we've got better success across our roster, but for the entirety of the season, better success at first base as well."

The idea that it's hard for players to perform in New York came up repeatedly. It was something Stearns acknowledged to be a truth, and that evaluating which free agents would be up for performing on the big stage is something he'll be considering more in the future.

"This is a unique place to play. It's different here," he said. "I've lived it as a fan, and as an executive, when you win here, it's the greatest thing in the world. There is nothing like coming to this ballpark in a playoff atmosphere and experiencing that. It's equally extreme when things aren't going well, and certain players struggle with that, and I'm cognizant of that."

Stearns said his vision of run prevention didn't work out too well, especially in the first half of the season.

"I think I'll retire the phrase run prevention. I don't know if that one wore particularly well," he said. "I think our pitching and defense was much better in the second half than we were in the first half."

Stearns answered in the affirmative when asked if the club needs more viable starting pitching, saying, "I do think it's necessary to add to our starting rotation. We can do that in a variety of different ways….Over the long term, what we need to do is develop pitchers at the top of our rotation, and I think we've proven we can do that….We also need to have more options, and we need the flexibility to go out and get those options when they're needed."

When asked how the club can prevent key injuries and make sure players coming off injury are ready to go, Stearns said reevaluating everything, including spring training ramp-ups, is on the table. "All of that is being looked at, and I imagine there will be some changes in how we do some of that," he said.

When asked about which way Bo Bichette was leaning regarding his player option, he said, "I have not had those discussions with Bo. He's got the right now to take some space and discuss things with his family and his agent. I'm sure he'll get back to us."

Stearns was once again noncommittal regarding hiring a general manager, but praised the recent addition of Derek Falvey to the front office. Similarly, he said he would discuss coaching staff additions with Green in the coming days.

Stearns said that the club will evaluate Kodai Senga 's role on the team during next year's spring training. "We need a level of production in whatever role he's going to be in to contribute to a winning team."

When asked about the plans for the back end of the bullpen, Stearns praised Devin Williams ' work to get healthy and get some innings in before the end of the season. "He's healthy, he feels great, and we expect him to be a big part of the back end going forward. We also feel good about the younger guys that stepped up in the last few months in a big way."

Stearns said that Tylor Megill and Reed Garrett are progressing in their recovery from elbow surgery and that both have been around the team recently, with the expectation of being available to compete in spring training.

Stearns confirmed that Ronny Mauricio is still considered to be in the mix as an infield option moving forward. "We saw the flash of potential over the last couple of days. That was exciting for us to see, and I think it was great for him to experience heading into the offseason….I think he comes into spring training next year competing for a spot."

When asked what the team could do to take the next step and be contenders, he said, "There's the continued maturation and growth of (our young) group, there is more consistent play and more available play from a group of veterans that we think is really good, and then there's whatever external acquisitions we bring in this offseason, along with the upper level of our (farm) system that we believe will contribute in a meaningful way this offseason."

articles.title: Bucs vs. Packers odds: Opening lines for Week 4 matchup
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are home once again Sunday as they welcome the Green Bay Packers to Raymond James Stadium. Both teams enter the matchup looking to g...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are home once again Sunday as they welcome the Green Bay Packers to Raymond James Stadium. Both teams enter the matchup looking to get things turned around following rough starts to the season. So what are the oddsmakers thinking of the Week 4 matchup between the Bucs and Packers?

Per FanDuel , Tampa Bay opens as a 3.5-point underdog at home for the fourth week of the 2026 regular season.

Point spread: Bucs +3.5 (-110) Point total: 39.5 Moneyline: Bucs +152, Packers -180

The Buccaneers are coming off a 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , dropping them to 0-3 on the season. Making matters worse, quarterback Baker Mayfield suffered a dislocated right thumb in the loss and is expected to miss at least three weeks, leaving rookie Jalon Daniels in line to make his first NFL start against Green Bay .

The Packers have struggled themselves, falling to 1-2 following an ugly 35-14 home loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday night. Green Bay's offense has had difficulty finding consistency early in the season, but Tampa Bay's quarterback situation has helped push the opening line in the Packers' favor.

The Bucs will now try to avoid an 0-4 start while Daniels attempts to give Tampa Bay a spark with Mayfield sidelined.

The game between the Bucs and Packers is scheduled for Sunday with kickoff set for 1:00 PM ET.

articles.title: See where Springfield area boys, girls golf teams go for regionals
articles.summary: With the IHSA girls and boys golf regionals beginning this week, this is a look at where teams in the SJ-R's coverage area are heading this postseason.
articles.body:
Our best photos from the Women's Professional Baseball League season

With the Illinois High School Association girls and boys golf regionals beginning this week, this is a look at where teams in The State Journal-Register's coverage area are heading this postseason.

Girls regionals , in the IHSA's two-class system, are Tuesday, Sept. 29. Boys regionals , a part of a three-class system, are Wednesday. Sectionals for boys and girls are Monday, Oct. 5 with the IHSA state finals held the weekend of Oct. 9-10 at five different courses.

The girls state finals are held at Red Tail Run (1A) and Hickory Point (2A) golf courses in Decatur. The boys state finals are at Vista Prairie (1A), Weibring (2A) and The Den at Fox Creek (3A) golf courses in Bloomington-Normal.

How do teams and individuals advance? In regionals, the top three teams advance to sectionals. If multiple teams tie for third place, ties will be broken. The top 10 individuals not on qualifying teams will also advance, but ties for 10th place will be determined with an on-course playoff.

In sectionals, the top three teams (ties will be broken again) qualify for the state tournament. Top 10 players who didn't advance to state as part of a team will also qualify for state, and any ties for the final spot will be determined with an on-course playoff.

At state, the field will be reduced to the top eight teams (and ties), along with top 40 individuals (including ties) not on an advancing team, after the first day of action.

Here is the full breakdown of where everyone in our area will be playing this week.

Metamora qualifiers will advance to the Cambridge Sectional at Valley View Club Cambridge.

Petersburg PORTA, Taylorville, Monticello and Mattoon qualifiers will advance to the Rochester Sectional at Lincoln Greens Golf Course.

Carlyle qualifiers will advance to the Roxana Sectional at Belk Park Golf Course.

Normal U-High qualifiers will advance to the Normal West Sectional at Ironwood Golf Course.

Tri-Valley and Meridian qualifiers will advance to the Monticello Sectional at University of Illinois (Orange Course).

PORTA qualifiers will advance to the Peoria Sectional at Kellogg Golf Course.

Brown County and Mount Olive qualifiers will advance to the Waterloo Gibault Sectional at Annbriar Golf Course.

Marquette and Jacksonville qualifiers will advance to the Quincy Notre Dame Sectional at Spring Lake Country Club.

Collinsville qualifiers will advance to the O'Fallon Sectional at Stonewolf Golf Club.

articles.title: Morrison extends Bristol City stay until 2028
articles.summary: Bristol City wide player Elijah Morrison signs a new deal to stay at Ashton Gate until the summer of 2028.
articles.body:
Bristol City wide player Elijah Morrison has signed a new deal to stay at Ashton Gate until the summer of 2028.

The 20-year-old, who has been capped by England's Under-18s, has made five appearances for the Robins, four coming as a substitute in the Championship.

He made his first City start in the EFL Cup first round win over Milton Keynes Dons in August 2025 and spent part of last season on loan at National League side Forest Green Rovers.

"Elijah is a great talent and one we're excited to keep at the club," head coach Michael Skubala told the club website.

"He's energetic, hard-working and deserving of a new contract. It's a big opportunity for him and we're excited to support his journey and see how far he can go."

articles.title: Matt Fitzpatrick on Open de France victory, his 'best period of golf' ever and Alfred Dunhill Links Championship hopes
articles.summary: Speaking on the Sky Sports Golf podcast, Matt Fitzpatrick discussed his FedEx Open de France victory, his impressive 2026 form and a strong start to the Ryder Cup qualification campaign, plus he looked ahead to playing alongside his father at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship
articles.body:
Fitzpatrick registered a fourth worldwide win of the season with a three-shot victory at the FedEx Open de France on Sunday, having already won three times on the PGA Tour during an impressive campaign.

The Englishman failed to finish higher than 14th in any of the majors in 2026 but still had six worldwide top 10s along with his victories, with Fitzpatrick proud of his season and contending so frequently.

"This is the best period of golf I've played for sure," Fitzpatrick told the Sky Sports Golf podcast . "2022 was right up there, but I've had three wins and obviously a fourth now. I think just the sustained consistency has been the big thing really.

"Obviously that [a disappointing major season] is a disappointment. It's the goal of anyone's at the start of the year to contend in the majors - those are what mean the most and those are what matter.

"It's disappointing not to do that this year. Just felt a couple days off pretty much during three of the four, then in the last one I just didn't play great and I got my strategy wrong.

"At the same time, that doesn't really take anything away from the season as a whole. I have contended a lot in a lot of golf tournaments and that's all you could ask for in a year."

Fitzpatrick's latest victory moved him top of the Ryder Cup qualification standings and inside the top 10 in the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai rankings, while the 32-year-old could move to a career-high world No 2 with a strong showing in Scotland.

When asked on whether there are areas where he can still improve, Fitzpatrick added: "I think there's various bits and pieces that we've looked at. We're coming to the year end and making those decisions on what the off-season plan needs to be.

"There's a few things that we've got down already to go to - it's just about how you go about that and how that's structured."

Fitzpatrick previously won the 2023 Alfred Dunhill Links Championship with his mother Sue as his partner in the pro-am team event, with Fitzpatrick teaming up with dad Russell for this year's contest.

"I think he might get a few more strokes - he'd probably say that himself!" admitted Fitzpatrick, who also won the Zurich Classic of New Orleans alongside his brother Alex Fitzpatrick in April.

"We're going to need a big few days I think, to get us in some form of position. Hopefully, Johan [Rupert, tournament organiser] doesn't cut his handicap too much after this past week!

"I think he's been playing quite nicely, so you never know - when the pressure's on, it can be a little bit different, but we're there to have a good time and enjoy ourselves."

Listen to the full Matt Fitzpatrick interview on the latest edition of the Sky Sports Golf podcast, hosted every week by Jamie Weir. Subscribe now on Apple Podcasts , Spotify or Spreaker , while vodcast editions can be found on the Sky Sports Golf YouTube channel .

Who else is playing the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship?

Matt's brother Alex is partnering mum Sue in the team element of this year's event, played across Carnoustie, Kingsbarns Golf Links and the Old Course at St Andrews.

Scotland's Robert MacIntyre returns as defending champion, while Tommy Fleetwood, Tyrrell Hatton and Justin Rose are other Ryder Cup players in the field, with Brooks Koepka and Cam Smith among the past major winners also in action.

Who will win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship? Live coverage begins Thursday from midday on Sky Sports Golf. Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW .

articles.title: Patrick Fishburn chasing 2027 PGA Tour security in home state of Utah
articles.summary: Utah native Patrick Fishburn hopes to secure his 2027 PGA Tour status at the Bank of Utah Championship this week.
articles.body:
Patrick Fishburn's 2026 season looked like it might be headed nowhere fast. The Utah native missed six cuts in his first eight starts, putting himself in an early hole. Since then, though, the BYU product has flipped the script, reaching the weekend in nine of his last 11 events and giving himself a legitimate chance to play his way into full PGA Tour status for 2027.

The next opportunity comes close to home at the Bank of Utah Championship.

The good news for Fishburn is that his game is trending in the right direction. The challenge is making sure he doesn't let the moment become bigger than the tournament itself. Playing in his home state, in front of family, friends and plenty of familiar faces, has brought added emotions in the past. This week, as he tries to keep his late-season surge alive, staying level-headed may be just as important as anything he does between the ropes.

"I've always loved St. George," Fishburn said. "I've been coming down here probably since I was 8 or 9 years old. I remember playing my first ever Utah Junior Golf Association event at Dixie Red Hills when I was about 9 years old. I remember being so nervous to play in it ... that tournament that I couldn't even tee the ball up. St. George has always been a fun place to come down to. Especially for us northern Utah guys, we like coming down to St. George. But it's a special place and I love the state of Utah, I love playing in front of friends and family, so this week's really awesome for me."

Fishburn is one of many players with local ties during this week's event at Black Desert Resort. Now in its third year on the PGA Tour schedule, the event has given the Utah contingent a chance to shine. Beehive State natives Rhett Rasmussen and Carson Lundell got into the field through Monday qualifying and BYU's Kihei Akina got in through a sponsor's exemption.

"It's really cool. It's really cool to see the level Utah golf is at. It's kind of just a nice nod to the Utah Junior Golf Association, the PGA Junior Section, Utah Golf Association, all these associations that I grew up playing in that has developed all these great players. So it's awesome," Fishburn said. "There's very talented. I know we had a couple more Utah guys get through the Monday qualifier yesterday, so I think there's probably 10 or, 10 maybe Utah players and they're all amazing college players, high school players, and so the state of Utah golf is really good.

"There's a lot of guys that can get to the PGA Tour and excited to see what they do, for sure."

And then, of course, is the golf course. Opened in 2023, Black Desert was the last course designed by Tom Weiskopf before his death from pancreatic cancer. Phil Smith, Weiskopf's partner in golf architecture, finished the job.

The layout has quickly climbed the rankings and is No. 1 in Utah on Golfweek's Best list of public-access courses, No. 30 among all resort courses in the U.S. and No. 101 among all modern courses in the country.

There have been a few hiccups with pace of play at this event since the rocks make it difficult to find strays

"First of all, it's beautiful. We don't have anything like this on Tour, probably in the world. You don't see features like this anywhere. The course is, it's very tricky. It's very intimidating off the tee. You can't see some of the landing areas, so you're picking targets on the hillside and just trying to trust your swing. So that's a challenge," Fishburn said. "Then I feel like these greens are very tricky. Very rarely do you have a pitch that just breaks one way. So you have to factor in a 10-, 15-footer and it's going to break both ways, and so it's really important to have your speed correct so it's catching both those breaks.

"But it's such a great test. I think my fellow players, PGA Tour players, I've heard nothing but great reviews and great things about coming here to St. George."

Tim Schmitt is the managing editor of Golfweek and the golf coordinator for the USA Today Network.

articles.title: Dolphins bring back DL-turned-OL on their practice squad
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins are looking for more offensive line depth, so they've brought back a familiar face on Tuesday.
articles.body:
After releasing defensive end Clelin Ferrell and defensive lineman Jordan Miller on Monday, the Miami Dolphins had two open spots on their practice squad, but they just filled one of them as they signed offensive lineman James Ester.

Ester spent five years at Northern Illinois from 2019-23. He recorded 121 tackles, nine sacks, six passes defensed, two forced fumbles, one fumble recovery and one interception. He signed with the Green Bay Packers as an undrafted free agent in 2024.

After spending two years in Green Bay on the defensive line and working with Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley, who was their defensive coordinator, he joined Miami's roster this offseason and switched to offensive line.

Ester didn't have a ton of success moving to guard, and he was eventually waived with an injury designation. The two sides agreed to an injury settlement that made him a free agent, and now he's back on the Dolphins' practice squad.

articles.title: Eagles News: An undesirable new franchise record
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 9/30/26.
articles.body:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Zero takeaways through three games. Not great! In fairness, the Birds have forced a couple fumbles that were recovered by the offense. So, some bad luck there. And with luck being an element in the turnover equation, the Eagles are probably due for some moving forward. That's the optimistic spin. The less rosy view of this situation is that the Eagles might not have enough playmakers to come up with these takeaways.

Let's get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

How is it possible to play three entire football games without forcing a turnover? That's where the Eagles are. This is the first time in franchise history the Eagles have opened a season without a takeaway in their first three games. They're only the 16th NFL team to ever achieve that dubious distinction. Of the first 15, only two reached the playoffs – the 1979 Broncos and 2004 Rams . There have been four previous seasons where the Eagles only forced one turnover through Week 3 – 1996, 1998, 2020 and 2021. This is also only the fourth time the Eagles haven't intercepted a pass through Week 3. That also happened in 1998, 2020 and 2021. The Eagles have now gone 13 consecutive games without multiple interceptions, the 6th-longest streak in franchise history and the 4th-longest current streak in the NFL. They haven't had a three-interception game since 2022, and their streak of 65 consecutive games without more than two INTs is by far the longest in franchise history. The next-longest streak is 34 games over the 2019 through 2021 seasons. The 65-game streak is 13th-longest in NFL history. Last time the Eagles picked off three passes in a game was Week 6 of the 2022 season, when C.J. Gardner-Johnson had two and Slay had one off Cooper Rush in a 26-17 win over the Cowboys at the Linc. The Eagles are 1-27-1 in their last 29 games when they're minus-three or worse in turnover differential. The Eagles are also only the fifth team with no takeaways and three or fewer sacks through Week 3 since sacks became an official stat in 1982. The four others: The 2002 Bengals , 2013 Steelers , 2019 Broncos and 2023 Giants. None of them made the playoffs.

It brings me no joy to say this, but I think what we saw on Monday night is closer to what this defensive unit actually is, and the elite Week 1 and Week 2 numbers are the fluke. The smoking gun for this theory is how bad Washington and Tennessee 's offenses are. The Commanders are 27th in pass offense and the Titans are 30th in scoring, 31st in total offense, and 30th in pass offense. Those are two bad teams, which is why the Eagles looked nice against them. But when facing Chicago 's actually-good offense — which ranks 3rd in total yards (408.0 YPG) and 1st in rushing (184.3 YPG) — the Eagles got exposed. They had no pass rush, they couldn't create turnovers, and they allowed Case Keenum of all people to sling the ball wherever he wanted. And sadly, these seem like foundational issues to me. Through three weeks, the Eagles have no takeaways. They have 3 sacks. No need to overcomplicate it. That's a bad defense.

This was a deeply disappointing offensive performance. There were positives on film, and I do not want to ignore them. However, those positives existed within an offense that still doesn't fit together. Right now, the Eagles look like they are running two separate offenses. They have a shotgun passing game and an under center running game. Those two worlds barely connect. The Eagles ran for 107 yards on 19 attempts, but that success didn't produce the explosive play-action passes it should. The numbers were ugly. The Eagles finished with 14 first downs and 248 net yards. They went 2-for-9 on third down, 0-for-5 on third-and-long, and 0-for-2 on fourth down. They reached the red zone twice and came away empty once. Andy Dalton 's interception was the single biggest win-probability swing of the game. We will get into that because I'm still angry… For me, the biggest problem was pass protection, particularly against pressure. I'm saying pass protection rather than offensive line play. Cam Jurgens had a poor game in pass protection, but the recurring free rushers were not simply five linemen losing individual blocks. The Eagles repeatedly looked confused about who they wanted to block and which defender they were prepared to leave free. That is a schematic and coaching problem first. Jalen Hurts was largely fine for three quarters before his play deteriorated once the Eagles fell behind by 20. The quarterback was not the main reason this offense failed.

Last week brought chaos to the NFC East as the Washington Commanders shocked the reigning champions to change everything we thought about them. Elsewhere in the division… the Dallas Cowboys collapsed against the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil. All the while the New York Giants took care of business against the Tennessee Titans … and then got a new quarterback in JJ McCarthy! Finally, the Philadelphia Eagles were expoed on Monday night by the Chicago Bears and Case Keenum of all people. Needless to say… RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton have a lot to discuss! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed!

So what the coaching staff essentially did there was trade an opportunity for three shots into the end zone for one bite at the apple on a type of play that (a) hadn't worked all season, (b) didn't really even work when they got a favorable look for it and finally executed it well, and (c) was a risky call that had a high likelihood of burning the rest of the clock if it failed. "We had 19 seconds," Nick Sirianni said. "We had plenty of time to get it clocked or do what we did in that particular case. They were bringing a certain type of pressure there, and that screen was built into the call, and it worked out to be able to get the touchdown there. But with 19 seconds left you should be able to get another play off." What?! They were flat out unable to get their next intended play off, which was a spike to stop the clock. They never would have been able to execute that in time, or even come close, and really, they came within hundredths of a second within getting the snap off on the impromptu sneak. If Smith had been tackled, at, saaay, the 3 yard line instead of the 1, there's a pretty good chance that Hurts would not have made the split-second decision to sneak it from that far away, even if the result of the play showed that he got in easily from the 1. Like, what would that scenario have looked like? My guess is that Hurts' best bet would have been to take the snap and try to run around hoping a receiver got open in some kind of back yard improv play. Honestly, I'm almost kind of bummed that we didn't get to see it. Even though it ultimately worked, there is really no good argument for that screen call in that situation, and it's alarming to me that any 12 year old playing Madden would also recognize that.

You can't point to anything to get genuinely excited about. The offense is wildly inconsistent. The defense has underachieved. They only have 3 sacks and don't have a single takeaway. As bad as things might sound, this group still has a lot of potential. It won't shock me to see them turn things around and start playing at a high level. Multiple experts picked this team to win the Super Bowl for a reason. The flip side is that I can also see things going sideways and this being a disappointing season. I don't get good vibes from this team. But I also had serious questions in 2024 and that group became a juggernaut once they got past the slow start. The Rams come to Philly on Sunday. They are 1-2 and coming off a highly frustrating loss. Sirianni, his coaches and the players better come up with some answers in a hurry or the Eagles could find themselves 2-2 with things getting crazy in a hurry.

This is the rare loss that seems even worse than when I left the stadium. Reviewing the game and the data shows just how concerning this was for the Eagles. It was their first 20-point loss since the 2023 season and matched the lowest scoring output of the Nick Sirianni era. It was their least efficient offensive performance of the Sirianni era, based on EPA per drive. The team was listless, heavily penalized, and lacked answers on both sides. And this didn't happen against Patrick Mahomes — they faced a third-string quarterback who hadn't started a game in 1,009 days and a defense that allowed 37 points and 478 yards in Week 1. "I think we all have to own that loss right there," Sirianni said. "I don't think anybody coached well. I don't think anyone played well. That was a true team loss. … I have to look at myself first. We weren't ready to coach, we weren't ready to play, and that ultimately starts and ends with me." My view with any loss is that it counts the same whether it's by 20 points or two points, so be careful about conflating a bad loss with a bad team. (This perspective doesn't always endear me to the fan base, but it matters over the course of a four-month season.) The problem with this loss now is you cannot rely on the first two games for all the equity this group built. When the Eagles lost to the New York Giants on Thursday night last year, it was a night where everything went wrong. The Eagles were also the defending Super Bowl champions who beat the Kansas City Chiefs and the Rams in September last year. But this team lacks the carryover equity from last year, and the first two games didn't convince anyone of heavyweight status. The Eagles had festering offensive problems in the first two weeks, saved by Jalen Hurts' superb third-down performance, while the defense wasn't yet playing to its potential. Hurts' third-down magic faded on Monday. The defense looked overmatched against Case Keenum and overwhelmed by Ben Johnson. This is an experienced, calloused group. Let's see how they respond.

Dontayvion Wicks had a disappointing Monday night in a game that saw the Eagles generally struggle, but he's still averaging a strong 2.3 yards per route run and carries a 31.2% air-yards share. He's a high-priority pickup for the future.

The Eagles' visit included wide receiver Darius Cooper , Eagles cheerleaders and team mascot Swoop. The organization also announced a $10,000 donation supporting the American Heart Association's CPR education and lifesaving training efforts.

One can attempt to mistakenly place blame for the Los Angeles Rams' 1-2 start on either injuries or officiating. The real reason for LA's shortcomings are the fact that their key players are not performing at star levels. Matthew Stafford has objectively been one of the worst quarterbacks in football so far. He's certainly better than that and will likely rebound at some point. Colby Parkinson is on a milk carton instead of the box score. The offensive line has overall taken a step back in pass protection. Kobie Turner , Braden Fiske , Byron Young , and even Aaron Donald have disappointed on the defensive line. Nate Landman still hasn't regained his early season magic from a year ago. For right now let's focus on the Rams' anemic passing attack.

Beckham's usage (or lack thereof) on offense had observers wondering what he was even doing on the team, considering he doesn't play special teams. In releasing Beckham, the Giants are now only carrying three wide receivers on their 53-man roster: Malik Nabers , Darnell Mooney , and rookie Malachi Fields .

There are many things to be pleased with. Prescott continues to roll, and the defense continues to tease us by flashing its upside. But even amidst these showings, this team can't do what they have failed to do in the past. Win at big moments. They had this game for the taking, but flamed out in the most Cowboys way. And the bad thing is a lot of this could have been avoided. Better play-calling at the goal line and more attention given to fend off the Ravens' offensive strength would have put them over the top to come away with the win. Until they can show they are capable of that, they'll always be the team that comes up a tad short.

The Commanders announced on Tuesday evening that guard Sam Cosmi (concussion/throat) and safety Nick Cross (illness/internal injury) will not make the trip, and have therefore been ruled out this week. Cosmi ended last season on IR due to a concussion and then suffered another one, along with a throat injury, from a nasty friendly-fire hit from rookie RB Kaytron Allen at the end of the Cowboys game in Week 2.

Ben Johnson, born in 1986, grew up in the heyday of the Madden era. Johnson's signature style of play calling has always seemed heavily indebted to the way someone would play video game football, with aggressive fourth down calls, intricate passing designs, and a love of mobile quarterbacks. The Chicago Bears head coach couldn't hide a smile when a reporter asked if he ever played Madden as a younger man last season.

articles.body: Ya puedes disfrutar del nuevo número de MARCA Plus, la revista oficial del Open de España presented by Madrid 2026. Una edición especial e interactiva con todo lo necesario para preparar una de las grandes citas del golf europeo, que se celebrará del 8 al 11 de octubre en el Club de Campo Villa de Madrid. Open de España presented by Madrid. DISFRUTA DEL NÚMERO GRATIS EN TU MÓVIL, TABLETA O PC El Open de España presenta un año más un cartel repleto de grandes nombres. Jon Rahm regresa con el objetivo de conquistar su cuarto título, mientras Sergio García vuelve a una competición que forma parte de su historia desde hace casi tres décadas. A ellos se une el vigente campeón, Marco Penge, que defenderá la corona conseguida en 2025. Open de España presented by Madrid. En este nuevo MARCA Plus podrás conocer precisamente a Penge en una entrevista exclusiva en la que recuerda el playoff que le llevó a la victoria y explica qué supone regresar al escenario donde cambió su carrera. También ponemos el foco en algunas de las grandes figuras internacionales que estarán en Madrid, con perfiles de Shane Lowry, Tyrrell Hatton, Bubba Watson, Francesco Molinari y Patrick Reed, además de una amplia representación española que buscará hacerse fuerte en casa. El especial recorre también algunas de las historias que han convertido al Open de España en uno de los torneos con mayor tradición del calendario. Madrid será una de las paradas del camino hacia Adare Manor para varios jugadores habituados a defender los colores de Europa. articles.title: Port Talbot lawyer who represented drug dealer jailed for selling cocaine
articles.summary: Ben Garvey passed messages between his drug dealer client and a drug runner before getting caught.
articles.body:
The criminal defence solicitor of a drug dealer has been jailed for three years and six months after he became involved in supplying cocaine.

Ben Garvey, 38, encouraged his friends to purchase the class A drug over WhatsApp, and also passed messages between his client and a drug runner.

Garvey, from Port Talbot, was told by a judge at Bristol Crown Court that his actions had been "a clear abuse" of his position, after he was found guilty of supplying cocaine and perverting the course of justice.

His ex-client, Daniel Baker, 34, was jailed for three years and four months after pleading guilty to perverting the course of justice and admitting conspiracy to supply Class A drugs.

Baker's drug runner, Jake Blackburn, 28, was jailed for four years and 10 months after being found guilty of perverting the course of justice, having previously pleaded guilty to being concerned in the supply of Class A drugs.

Garvey had been a partner at David W Harris Solicitors & Co based in Swansea, Pontypridd, and Talbot Green, and had met Baker in 2021 after purchasing cocaine from him.

The court heard he later represented Baker when he was arrested on suspicion of dealing drugs, and passed on messages between Baker and his drug runner Blackburn during his client's time in custody.

Prosecutor Ray Tully KC said: "The police investigation into Mr Baker led them to realise Mr Baker was involved in a drugs operation in south Wales, where he comes from, and there was an Oxford angle. He was sourcing and supplying drugs in the Oxford area."

Tully said another message from Blackburn to Garvey asked for Baker's iCloud username and password, which he said was so Blackburn could "delete or wipe information online" and "take care of things after the boss had been nicked".

"In the circumstances, the prosecution suggest the communication that took place is evidence they were all involved in relaying information to and from Mr Baker whilst he was in custody," Tully said.

"We say that it's an attempt to preserve and protect the drugs operation and carry on business whilst the boss is incarcerated, and the communication would be designed to hamper and impede the investigation that has got under way that day."

As a result of messages discovered on Baker's phone, Garvey and Blackburn were arrested and their electronic devices were seized.

Messages on Garvey's phone revealed he had been part of a WhatsApp group in which he encouraged and "egged on" friends to purchase cocaine. Images taken from the group included photos and videos of people using the drug.

Garvey was found guilty of perverting the course of justice, being concerned in the supply of Class A and C drugs, and encouraging or assisting in the commission of an offence.

Judge Cullum told Garvey while he had previously been "a hardworking and qualified solicitor" he had "found kudos by being around high status criminals".

The judge said he had "let down the whole profession of solicitors whose professionalism and diligence the criminal justice system depends on daily".

"It is a sad day for you today to be sentenced in a crown court," he said.

articles.title: Justin Thomas net worth in 2026: Inside  the leading American golfer’s career, earnings, endorsements and more
articles.summary: Justin Thomas has built a successful career as one of the leading American golfers of his generation.
articles.body: Justin Thomas has built a successful career as one of the leading American golfers of his generation. The Louisville native turned professional in 2013 after a standout college career with the Alabama Crimson Tide. He established himself on the PGA Tour and became a regular contender in major events.Thomas enjoyed his biggest breakthrough in 2017. He won five PGA Tour events that year, including the PGA Championship. He also captured the FedEx Cup. His success continued in the following years, with more major victories, PGA Tour titles and appearances for the United States in the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup.Justin Thomas’ net worth in 2026 Justin Thomas has an estimated net worth of $55 million (per celebrity net worth). His wealth comes from PGA Tour prize money, bonuses, endorsement deals, business ventures and other investments.Thomas has earned more than $71.3 million in official PGA Tour prize money as of early 2026. His total on-course earnings are even higher when FedEx Cup bonuses, Player Impact Program payments and unofficial event earnings are included.His 2017 season was particularly important financially. After winning the FedEx Cup, Thomas received a reported $10 million bonus. He has also received several multi-million-dollar payments through the PGA Tour’s Player Impact Program.Endorsements are another major source of income for Thomas. He has long-standing partnerships with Titleist and FootJoy. His other corporate partners have included Citi, NetJets and Rolex.Thomas has also developed business interests away from professional golf. In 2022, he founded WearSPF, a sun protection brand inspired by his own experience with melanoma. The business focuses on sun safety and protection.He has also moved into golf course design. Thomas partnered with Jack Nicklaus on Panther National, a luxury golf and residential development in Palm Beach County, Florida.Thomas impressed by winning the Dell Technologies Championship and CJ Cup. His results helped him secure the 2017 FedEx Cup.He reached No. 1 in the Official World Golf Ranking in 2018. He won the Honda Classic and WGC-Bridgestone Invitational that year. He returned to the top of the rankings in 2020 after winning the WGC-FedEx St. Jude Invitational.In 2022, Thomas won his second PGA Championship. He later ended a winless stretch on the PGA Tour by capturing the RBC Heritage in 2025.Thomas has also represented the United States at several major team competitions. He has been part of winning Ryder Cup teams in 2018, 2021 and 2023. He also helped the United States win the Presidents Cup in 2017, 2019 and 2022.His success on the course has been matched by his property investments. Thomas previously owned a home in Jupiter, Florida, which he bought for about $1.5 million in 2016 and sold for $3.1 million in 2022.He later purchased a waterfront property in Tequesta, Florida, for approximately $13.45 million. articles.title: Nanded & Latur collectors ban movement of green, dry fodder outside districts amid shortage concerns
articles.summary: Nanded and Latur collectors ban sale and transport of green/dry fodder outside district limits amid drought and below-average monsoon, to conserve local stocks.
articles.body: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: Nanded and Latur district administrations have prohibited the sale and transportation of green and dry fodder, grass and cattle feed outside their limits amid concerns of a fodder shortage following below-average monsoon rainfall.In Nanded, collector Rahul Kardile issued the order on Tuesday and the restrictions took effect on Wednesday. In Latur, collector and district disaster management authority chairman Dr Bharat Bastewad issued the order under the Disaster Management Act, 2005. The restrictions will remain in force in both the districts until further notice.“The administration has decided to conserve the fodder currently available in the district for local livestock in view of the prevailing situation. The restriction applies to green and dry fodder, grass and cattle feed and prohibits their sale, as well as transportation outside Nanded district,” Kardile said.The move follows the state’s drought declaration in 265 talukas under Trigger-1 for the 2026 kharif season. In Nanded, 14 of the district’s 16 talukas have been declared drought-affected, with only Mudkhed and Mukhed excluded.According to the administration, rainfall in the district remained below average this monsoon, raising concerns over reduced agricultural output and fodder production. “Anticipating a shortage in the coming months, it has been decided to conserve available fodder stocks for local livestock,” a district official said.Issued under the Maharashtra Fodder (Export Control) Order, 2001, the directive instructs authorities to immediately enforce the restriction and prevent movement of fodder beyond district limits. The administration said the order was part of preparations to mitigate the impact of drought conditions and safeguard fodder supplies for local requirements.Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news.
